text:
olivia: Ran an Nsight Systems capture for the KV prefetch path — attaching the .nsys in the artifact store: s3://profiles/1758123456.nsys. Timeline looks noisy, curious if this is memcpy vs kernel overlap or CPU launch lag.

martin: quick skim — I see H2D async chunks on the copy-engine stream interleaving with small decode kernels on the compute stream. But there's a 8–12ms gap between the memcpy end and the next kernel executing. Screenshot: https://img.internal/1758123456/timeline.png :eyes:

rebecca: can you paste the timeline text snippet? also did you use pinned host memory for async copies? if not cudaMemcpyAsync will fallback to staged sync copies.

olivia: pasted minimal timeline below. capture was with our default workload (batch size distribution matching prod). we did not force pinned mem for that run.

```
Stream 0 (compute): kernel_decode_A 0.2ms -> 11.7ms
Stream 2 (copy)  : H2D_async_chunk_1 3.1ms -> 9.8ms
CPU (enqueue)    : queue_kernel_B at 11.2ms -> kernel_B actually starts 21.6ms
Observed gap: ~10.4ms between enqueue and kernel start
```

diego: that gap smells like CPU scheduling / launch thread blocked. Two quick checks: 1) ensure the host pointer is pinned (cudaHostAlloc) or use cudaMemcpyAsync with pinned; 2) run `perf record -e sched:sched_switch -aR` while replay to look for preemption.

martin: also confirm which stream priorities/affinities are used. If copy engine is saturating PCIe, kernel might still queue but get delayed by driver work. nvtx shows the kernel queued on the device but driver delayed actual dispatch.

rebecca: oh and check for accidental `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` in the path between the two ops. Even logging code or an error-check macro can introduce a blocking sync.

olivia: good calls. i re-ran with pinned mem and a lighter logging build. gap reduced to ~1.2ms. upload: s3://profiles/1758123456-pinned.nsys.

martin: nice. another angle: capture CPU-side with `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,os —sample=cpu` and look for the host thread being preempted. i saw similar on an m60 cluster where kube throttling moved the worker thread and launch latency spiked.

sre-oncall: fyi infra-bot says the node had a kube eviction event around 1758123500 on that host — possible noisy neighbors. infra-bot:eviction: `node/worker-12 had kubelet memory pressure, pods OOMKilled`

diego: if this is reproducible, try pinning the launcher thread to a reserved core (taskset) or use real-time scheduling for the inference process. we moved the launcher to an isolated cpuset in staging and saw ~25–35% lower tail latency on kernel launch.

rebecca: aside — when you used pinned mem did you also try `cudaMemcpyAsync(..., cudaMemcpyHostToDevice)` on a dedicated copy stream (cudaStreamCreateWithPriority) so the copy engine doesn't contend with other copies?

olivia: yes, created a dedicated copy stream and separate compute stream per worker. that plus pinned mem gave the best result. still seeing occasional 0.8–1.5ms spikes; i'll follow up with a capture that includes `--trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt` and the perf sched_switch output.

martin: TL;DR: observed interleaving is expected, but the big gaps were mostly host-side scheduling + non-pinned host buffers. fixes: pinned host buffers, dedicated copy stream, reserve a CPU for launcher thread. next step: long-run capture (10k inferences) to validate tail behavior.

olivia: thanks. i'll run long capture overnight and leave notes here. ping @diego @rebecca if I need help parsing the perf trace. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://profiles/1758123456-longrun.nsys (size: 120MB)

sre-oncall: added incident tag `perf-investigation-1758123456` for tracking, assigning to infra eng-runtime on Monday.
